Building Distributed Caches with Consistent Hashing

By Marcus Vance

When scaling stateful caching tiers across dynamic clusters, traditional modular hashing schemes create severe operational headaches during node churn. Adding or removing a single node forces nearly all keys to remap, triggering cache stampedes.

The Consistent Hashing Ring

Consistent hashing solves this remapping catastrophe by mapping both cache nodes and data keys to a circular numeric space, typically represented as a 32-bit or 64-bit integer ring.

// Example Hash Ring in JavaScript
class ConsistentHashRing {
  constructor(virtualNodes = 100) {
    this.virtualNodes = virtualNodes;
    this.ring = new Map();
    this.sortedKeys = [];
  }

  addNode(node) {
    for (let i = 0; i < this.virtualNodes; i++) {
      const hash = this.hashKey(`\${node}:\${i}`);
      this.ring.set(hash, node);
      this.sortedKeys.push(hash);
    }
    this.sortedKeys.sort((a, b) => a - b);
  }
}

By distributing virtual nodes uniformly around the ring, traffic remains balanced even when physical hardware nodes join or leave the topology dynamically.

In production workloads, consistent hashing maintains an average hit ratio above 96 percent during active node replacement, safeguarding database storage layers from sudden request spikes.
